title: Uniform and Typewriter
premise: In the river city of Vellamare, 1912, Tamsin Quintana secretly completes the master atlas her dead mentor died protecting, while a mysterious child left at the workshop door draws the attention of both the occupying garrison and the resistance. As the ice on the river thaws and the deadline for delivering the atlas approaches, Tamsin must choose between surrendering the work to save the child or finishing it at the cost of everything she loves. She finishes the atlas, smuggles it out with the child hidden in its traveling case, and burns the workshop behind her — surviving, but forever changed by what survival cost.
about_author: Ulyana Sandoval is a former cartographer's assistant who spent a decade restoring archival maps in coastal libraries before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for their meticulous period detail and quiet heroines whose hands remember what their hearts try to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She works alone in the frozen workshop, inking coastlines from her dead master's notes, keeping grief at bay through routine. Emotional beat: disciplined loneliness, the atlas as an unfinished conversation with the dead.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A hooded stranger leaves a sleeping child on the doorstep with a note: 'Forget this face.' The boy, Milo, cannot speak of where he came from. Emotional beat: fear cracking open into reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Garrison Calls
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A lieutenant inspects the workshop, asking pointed questions about her master's final commission. She lies smoothly for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: the low profile she built begins to cost her honesty.

chapters.title: Milo's Hands
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. The child watches Tamsin draw and recognizes the coastline he saw from a ship's rail. He says one word too many. Emotional beat: a child's guilt, the terror of having given something away.

chapters.title: What the Master Died For
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching her mentor's locked drawer, she finds letters revealing the atlas contains mapped fortifications the occupiers would kill to possess. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed from gift to burden.

chapters.title: The Ice Groans
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The river ice begins shifting early; the thaw that will let ships — and soldiers — move freely is weeks ahead of schedule. Emotional beat: time becoming an antagonist.

chapters.title: An Old Friend of the Workshop
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Resistance courier Odile arrives seeking the atlas for the cause, revealing Tamsin's master was more entangled than she knew. Emotional beat: betrayal and loyalty braided together.

chapters.title: Two Claims on One Map
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Odile wants the atlas; the garrison suspects it exists; Tamsin realizes finishing it serves everyone but herself. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of being the only keeper of a dangerous truth.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Drew Ships
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Milo sketches the warship he escaped from; Tamsin recognizes the harbor it anchors in — a page missing from the atlas. Emotional beat: the child becomes the map's missing key.

chapters.title: Lieutenant Voss Returns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Voss offers protection in exchange for the completed atlas, making clear what happens to harbors of fugitives when the ice breaks. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Nights of Two Inks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. By day Tamsin draws false plates for the garrison; by night the true atlas. Milo learns to grind pigments and keep secrets. Emotional beat: double life as intimacy — two people bound by shared deception.

chapters.title: Odile's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Odile gives her until the ice breaks to hand over the finished atlas, warning that the resistance protects its own — and no one else. Emotional beat: love against duty, with duty wearing a friend's face.

chapters.title: The Face Remembered
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss identifies Milo as the son of a hanged resistance leader and orders the workshop watched. Emotional beat: cold procedure hiding a flicker of doubt about the orders themselves.

chapters.title: What Survival Is Worth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A neighbor who sheltered knowledge of Milo is arrested; Tamsin sees the price others pay for her silence. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She inks the final plate — the harbor only Milo could describe — and holds the finished atlas, complete and lethal. Emotional beat: triumph curdled by dread; the work is done, now comes the reckoning.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. A workshop assistant, terrified for his family, tells Voss about the child. Soldiers surround the street. Emotional beat: innocence shattered, the noose closing.

chapters.title: The Burning Question
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Cornered, Tamsin strikes her bargain: a decoy atlas for safe passage out of the city before the ice breaks. Voss, half-sympathetic, accepts — but someone else is listening. Emotional beat: desperate negotiation, hope with a hairline crack.

chapters.title: Ice Breaking
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The river cracks open; Odile's cell moves to seize the atlas themselves, believing Tamsin will sell it. Guns come to the workshop. Emotional beat: every debt called at once.

chapters.title: The Atlas Leaves Without Me
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the chaos, Tamsin hides Milo inside the atlas's great traveling case and slips him to Odile's smugglers, staying behind as decoy. Emotional beat: the climax of sacrifice — giving away both the work and the boy she loves.

chapters.title: Fire on Quay Street
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Interrogated by Voss, she watches the workshop burn — set by the resistance to destroy evidence. Voss lets her go, unable to prove anything against a woman with ash on her hands. Emotional beat: devastation and strange mercy intertwined.

chapters.title: Northward
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. On a ship beyond the border, Milo opens the case: the true atlas, which Tamsin swapped for the decoy at the last moment, wrapped around a letter in her hand. Emotional beat: the inheritance delivered; love proven by absence.

chapters.title: Uniform and Typewriter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, years later. Working as a typist under a new name, she receives a parcel: a published atlas, credited to her master, with Milo's drawing tucked inside. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — survival's price paid, its inheritance finally hers.
